name: Sap Ng Wu
description: Sap Ng Wu (十五湖) is a climbing game for three or four players using an 84-card Chinese domino pack. Players in turn beat the previous play with a higher card or combination or pass; the player who played the highest takes the cards as wu (winning cards). The first to collect 15 or more wu declares a win (sik wu) and receives chip payments from the others.

setup.deck:
Type: 84-card Chinese domino pack (十五湖紙牌); 21 tile types with four copies of each
Jokers: Not included
setup.dealing: Pack shuffled and spread face down; players take one card at a time anticlockwise from dealer until all taken. Three players: 28 cards each; four players: 21 each.
setup.equipment:
84-card Chinese domino pack (15 lakes playing-cards)
Chips for payment (optional)
Table space

rules.objective: Be the first to collect 15 or more wu (winning cards) and declare a win (食湖 sik wu).
rules.gameplay:
1. Optional: Any player with a supreme combination (cards 2-4 and 1-2, at least one of each) may lay it face up; it counts as wu.
2. Dealer leads any card or valid combination face up.
3. In turn each player may beat the current play with a higher card or combination of the same count and suit mix, or pass.
4. When all but one pass in succession, that player takes the winning cards as wu and leads next.
5. First to have 15 or more wu may declare (sik wu); play ends and winner receives chip payments: 1 chip for 15-17 wu, 2 for 18-20, up to 5 for 27-28. A player may delay declaring to try for more wu but then must reach the next threshold to declare.
keyRules: Cards played singly or in sets of 2, 3, or 4 identical cards; sets beaten only by higher sets of same count and suit
Civil and military suits with mixed combinations; Heaven 6-6 with nines, supreme pair 2-4 and 1-2 is unbeatable
Four of a kind played and not beaten: each other player pays 1 chip immediately
Eight-card supreme (all four 2-4 and all four 1-2) counts as 16 wu

strategy.basic: Save high civil and military cards to beat key leads; lay supreme early if you have it to count wu.
strategy.intermediate: Track which ranks have been played; decide when to declare at 15 wu versus playing on for higher chip payouts.
strategy.advanced: Time declaration to maximise chips while avoiding another player declaring first; use four-of-a-kind for immediate chip gain.
tips: Delay declaring only if you can reach 18+ wu before others reach 15.
Supreme combination laid pre-play counts as wu; 8-card supreme is an instant 16 wu.

scoring.description: Each card or combination won counts as one wu. First to 15 or more wu may declare (sik wu). Chip payments: 1 for 15-17 wu, 2 for 18-20, 3 for 21-23, 4 for 24-26, 5 for 27-28. Four of a kind won: each opponent pays 1 chip. 8-card supreme counts as 16 wu.
